key_insight: ER70S-6 WAAM steel showed strong tensile anisotropy: strength was highest parallel to the bead direction, while flat builds behaved more consistently than upright builds.
engineering_relevance: Build orientation and load alignment should be considered when designing WAAM steel components for multidirectional loading.
method: Tensile testing at 0°, 45°, 60°, and 90° in flat and upright build configurations.
Two specimens tested per condition, with one representative result reported.
Hardness measurements and an empirical model of angle-dependent tensile strength.
evidence_signal: Upright-build ultimate tensile strength decreased approximately 47% at 45° versus 0°, while hardness variation was governed mainly by build direction.
watch_item: Representative-specimen reporting limits assessment of repeatability; interlayer shear and delamination remain proposed contributors rather than confirmed failure mechanisms.
paper_title: Effects of loading angle and build direction on the tensile behavior of WAAM steel produced with ER70S-6 welding wire
